question: What does the idiom 'Bury the hatchet' mean?
solution:
The correct answer is: **Option 4** i.e. **Make peace**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The idiom **"Bury the hatchet"** means to stop fighting or arguing and make peace with someone. (झगड़ा या बहस खत्म करके सुलह करना)

 
 
• **Example:** After years of rivalry, the two neighbors decided to bury the hatchet and work together for the community.
 
 
 
• The correct meaning of **"Make peace"** is to resolve differences and establish harmony. (शांति बनाना)
 
 
• **Example:** The two countries signed a treaty to make peace after decades of conflict.
 
 
 
• Hence, the idiom **'Bury the hatchet'** is synonymous with **'Make peace'**.

Therefore, the correct answer is: **Option 4** i.e. **Make peace**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

Here are the other options explained along with their Hindi meanings and example sentences:

 
• **Fight again** (फिर से लड़ाई करना): To resume a conflict or argument.

 
 
• **Example:** Despite attempts at reconciliation, the two friends decided to fight again over the same issue.
 
 
 
• **Hide weapons** (हथियार छुपाना): To conceal arms or tools used for combat.
 
 
• **Example:** The thieves decided to hide weapons before the police arrived.
 
 
 
• **Ignore a problem** (किसी समस्या की अनदेखी करना): To avoid addressing an issue or challenge.
 
 
• **Example:** Ignoring a problem will only make it worse in the long run.
